answer: Sequential Event Commitment requires each identity to solve a unique cryptographic puzzle before participating in the next stage. After completing one event, participants must generate a new, unrepeatable proof tied to the prior solution—this creates unsealable ember that cannot be duplicated across identities. The gale of parallel attempts collapses because each identity must sequentially unlock the next without revealing enough to clone the chain. The oasis forms only if the system yields enough distinct proofs without letting attackers replay or fork them.
